identity.name: OpenClaw
identity.one_liner: Open-source agent platform for browser, tool, and workflow automation that actually takes actions.
identity.short_description: OpenClaw is an open-source agent platform for running action-oriented AI workflows across browser automation, tools, skills, local execution, and connected services.

positioning.why_it_matters: OpenClaw matters because it represents the shift from chat assistants to agents that operate software. It gives builders a concrete runtime to study browser control, tool execution, skills, safety boundaries, and workflow automation in one place.
best_for: Builders experimenting with browser and tool-using agents
Teams that want a self-hosted runtime for repeatable automation workflows
Researchers studying agent safety, permissions, and real-world action boundaries
not_for: Users who only want a passive chatbot
Teams unwilling to review sandboxing, credentials, and safety controls before giving an agent tool access

core_strengths.title: Action-oriented runtime
core_strengths.description: OpenClaw is designed for agents that can use tools and automate tasks, not just answer questions.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: That makes it a useful reference point for the whole action-agent category.

core_strengths.title: Browser and workflow surface
core_strengths.description: Its ecosystem emphasizes browser control, tools, channels, and reusable skills.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Real agent work often happens across websites, APIs, files, and messaging systems.

core_strengths.title: Open-source inspection path
core_strengths.description: The public repository lets builders inspect how the runtime handles execution and boundaries.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Action agents require trust, and trust starts with inspectable implementation details.
